turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Sure. Let me think aloud with an example: "A train is ___ (fast) than a bus."
Step 1: "fast" is a short word, so I add -er: faster.
Step 2: I compare two things, so "than" comes next.
Result: "A train is faster than a bus."
Rule: add -er to a short word, put "more" before a long word, then use "than".
Right: "Ali is taller than Omar." Wrong: "Ali is more tall than Omar."
Your turn. Complete:
"Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
